body.statement: There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\), such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(h\le r_0\), and every \(1\le k\le m h^d\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same Hölder-radius restrictions as the primitive nuisances and \(\Pr_Q\{|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|>B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\}\le\eta\). The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.
body.justification: A uniform error envelope prevents coverage from being inferred by simply adding a Gaussian variance to a biased nonregular estimator.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
body.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish the finite-sample bias, degenerate-U-statistic fluctuation, and propagated Gaussian-noise bounds for an explicit estimator.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen construction contains no equations for \(\widehat Q\), \(\widehat R\), the quadratic kernel, pilot clipping, or noise scales.  The displayed \(B\), \(S\), and \(G\) envelopes name desired bounds but cannot serve as premises proving them.
obligation.attempted: I decomposed the envelopes into localization, cell approximation, linear fluctuation, quadratic fluctuation, and two privacy terms.  This verifies their tuning algebra but cannot verify that the unspecified random estimator has those remainders.
obligation.partial_result: If an explicit estimator satisfied the claimed deterministic bias bound and the two claimed stochastic bounds, their union would immediately give the displayed probability inequality.  The present construction does not specify the random variables to which concentration is to be applied.  In particular, no equation defines \(\widehat Q\), \(\widehat R\), the quadratic correction, pilot clipping, or Gaussian scales, so neither the degenerate \(U\)-statistic variance nor propagation through the stabilized inverse can be checked.  The algebraic envelope alone is not a proof of such properties.
